prompt: Write your own checked exception in ParseException.java, then use it in RecordParser.java to reject malformed "name,age" lines by line number -- while parseAll skips the bad lines and counts them.
explanation: Extending Exception (rather than RuntimeException) makes ParseException checked, so every caller must either catch it or declare it -- which is why parse() needs `throws ParseException` in its signature. Passing the message to super() keeps getMessage() working, while the extra lineNumber and lineText fields carry the context a plain message cannot. parse() also shows exception translation: it catches the low-level NumberFormatException from Integer.parseInt and rethrows it as the meaningful ParseException. parseAll then demonstrates the other half of the pattern -- catching the exception inside the loop so one bad record does not abort the whole batch.
hints: In ParseException, call super("line " + lineNumber + ": " + lineText) as the FIRST statement of the constructor, then assign the two fields.
line.split(",", -1) gives you the fields; the -1 keeps trailing empty pieces so "Ada," still splits into two, and you can check parts.length != 2 to reject the rest.

Wrap only the Integer.parseInt call in try/catch (NumberFormatException e) and throw a new ParseException from the catch block. In parseAll, the try/catch goes INSIDE the loop so it can keep going after a failure.
